9 MP global-shutter sensor with region HDR for four-lane traffic cameras.
9 MP global-shutter sensor for traffic cameras, successor to the SC910GS.
9 MP monochrome global-shutter sensor for industrial cameras.
15 MP 5K security sensor with 16:9 and 4:3 crops.
Early 720p Exmor security sensor found in the first Hi3518 and Hi3516C cameras.
A 12 MP still-and-4K sensor made for consumer camcorders and action cameras; it reads 4K at about 60 frame/s from a cropped area.
Sony's first 1080p sensor for low-cost IP cameras, front-illuminated; the IMX222 and IMX322 that followed keep its pixel and registers.
A 3 MP wide-dynamic-range security sensor of the Hi3516A generation.
Full HD security sensor of the early 2010s, readable at 120 frame/s in 1080p.
The 4:3 1.3 MP companion of the IMX104, used in early Hi3518 cameras.
The industrial version of the IMX117's 12 MP back-illuminated array, with 4K at 60 frame/s.
The first Pregius global-shutter sensor, large 5.86 µm pixels at up to 164 frame/s; also sold in monochrome.
A 6.4 MP back-illuminated sensor that crops 5 MP in 4:3, 5:4 or 16:9 for 1/2-type lenses; a monochrome version (IMX178LLJ) exists.
Large-pixel 1080p sensor known for low-light performance and a built-in WDR mode reaching about 100 dB.
An 8 MP mobile-class sensor best known from the Raspberry Pi Camera Module v2.
The back-illuminated successor of the IMX122 in the same footprint, common in cheap 1080p cameras.
A 1.3 MP back-illuminated sensor with large pixels, a low-light favourite of 960p cameras.
The 60 frame/s version of the IMX224, without its digital-overlap HDR.
A 12 MP back-illuminated sensor reading 4K at 60 frame/s; a monochrome version (IMX226CLJ) exists.
A 1080p security sensor with 2.8 µm pixels from the early 2010s, still found on older boards.
A 1.3 MP sensor with 3.75 µm pixels for 960p and 720p cameras.
The 30 frame/s, lower-cost sibling of the IMX174 with the same pixel.
A 12.4 MP 1.1-type global-shutter sensor, a staple of machine-vision cameras.
The 4K (17:9) version of the IMX253 in the same package.
A 5 MP 2/3-type global-shutter sensor with the 3.45 µm Pregius pixel.
A 3.2 MP global-shutter sensor for factory and traffic cameras; colour and monochrome versions exist.
An 8.5 MP back-illuminated 4K sensor with digital-overlap HDR, used in early 4K security and embedded cameras.
A 0.4 MP global-shutter sensor with very large 6.9 µm pixels for high-speed inspection.
The first STARVIS 1080p sensor and the reference for starlight cameras; a monochrome version (IMX290LLR) exists.
The IMX290 without digital-overlap HDR; only multiple-exposure WDR is offered.
A 4/3-type 4K security sensor with Quad Bayer pixels for single-frame HDR, popular in astronomy cameras.
The 23 frame/s, lower-bandwidth version of the IMX253's 12.4 MP global-shutter array.
The 60 frame/s cost-down of the IMX290 and one of the most common 2 MP starlight sensors in IP cameras.
A 1080p sensor for dash cams and consumer IP cameras with a parallel-only output.
The IMX322 in a smaller package, found in many budget 1080p cameras.
A 6.8 MP back-illuminated sensor that crops to 5 MP or 4 MP, used with the Hi3519V101.
A 60 frame/s STARVIS 1080p sensor with the same pixel, outputs and HDR modes as the IMX307.
An 8 MP 1/1.8-type 4K security sensor, the predecessor Sony compares the IMX678 against.
The most common 5 MP sensor in IP cameras; a monochrome version (IMX335LLN) exists.
A 4 MP sensor with large 2.9 µm pixels for low-light cameras; the IMX464 is its NIR-enhanced sibling.
A 12 MP sensor for consumer cameras that reads 4K at 60 frame/s, used in some Hi3516CV500 and Hi3519 designs.
A 1/2-type 1080p sensor with 3.75 µm pixels for ultra-low-light cameras.
A 12.3 MP stacked sensor for security cameras, closely related to the IMX477 and IMX577.
The common 4K (8 MP) sensor of 1/2.8-type IP cameras, with small 1.45 µm pixels.
A 61 MP full-frame sensor with 16-bit output, used mostly in astronomy and scientific cameras.
A pin-compatible IMX290 with markedly better near-infrared sensitivity, popular for night-vision cameras.
The NIR-enhanced version of the IMX347, a 4 MP low-light sensor.
A 12.3 MP stacked sensor best known from the Raspberry Pi High Quality Camera.
A 2 MP sensor whose 5.8 µm pixels are 2x2 binned from a 1/1.2-type array, built for extreme low light.
A 1/1.2-type 4K sensor with 2.9 µm pixels; Sony names it as the model the IMX585 improves on.
A compact BGA-packaged 4K sensor related to the IMX415, with better near-infrared response.
A square 9 MP 1-type sensor, mostly found in astronomy cameras.
A 26 MP APS-C sensor with 16-bit output, used in astronomy and scientific cameras.
A 12.3 MP stacked sensor of the IMX477 family used in drones, action cameras and Hi3519-class designs.
The first STARVIS 2 sensor, a 1/1.2-type 4K part that Sony rates at 88 dB in a single exposure (Clear HDR) and 106 dB with multiple exposures; a monochrome version (IMX585-AAMJ1) exists.
A 128 MP 3.6-type global-shutter sensor for large-area inspection.
A STARVIS 2 1080p sensor with 2.9 µm pixels that Sony rates at 88 dB in a single exposure using Clear HDR.
A 4 MP STARVIS 2 sensor with 2.9 µm pixels for low-light cameras; a monochrome version exists.
A 5 MP STARVIS 2 sensor that can stream a region of interest at high speed alongside the full frame; Sony quotes 78 dB dynamic range and about 30% less power than the IMX335.

sensitivity.note: 12-bit, IMX675-AAQR (15879 with the AR-coated AAQR1), Tj 60 °C

sensors.notes: A square 12.6 MP STARVIS 2 sensor made for fisheye and panoramic cameras.
The STARVIS 2 4K sensor at 1/1.8-type that replaces the IMX334 in newer 8 MP cameras.

sensitivity.note: 12-bit, IMX678-AAQR (16309 with the AR-coated AAQR1), Tj 60 °C

sensors.notes: A 4K 1/2.8-type sensor like the IMX415 with improved near-infrared sensitivity and an AR-coated cover glass.
A newer 4K 1/2.8-type sensor in the IMX715 class with an I2C/I3C control interface.
A 4K 1/2.8-type sensor like the IMX415 with an I2C/I3C control interface, also offered as a chip-scale package.

sensitivity.note: 12-bit, IMX779-AQR (5240 for the AQN chip-scale package), Tj 60 °C

sensors.notes: A 5 MP STARVIS 2 sensor with large 2.9 µm pixels and a Hybrid HDR mode combining Clear HDR with digital overlap; a monochrome version exists.
The 1080p STARVIS 2 sensor on Sony's current lineup, with 2.9 µm pixels for low light.

sensitivity.note: 12-bit, IMX832-AQR (19556 with the AR-coated AQR1), Tj 60 °C

sensors.notes: A 1/1.2-type 4K STARVIS 2 sensor in the IMX585 class with an AR-coated cover glass.
A 1/1.8-type 4K STARVIS 2 sensor in the IMX678 class with an AR-coated cover glass.
The first STARVIS 3 sensor, whose LOFIC pixels give 96 dB in a single 4K exposure (Clear HDR3) from small 1.45 µm pixels.
Common 1080p sensor in Xiongmai and other budget IP cameras; it is the same die as the OmniVision OV2735, and both report chip ID 0x2735.

sensitivity.note: from the OV2735 datasheet, the same die

sensors.notes: 2K security sensor with large 2.9 µm pixels, Nyxel NIR and DCG HDR (90 dB from one exposure); the same silicon OmniVision later sold as the OS04J10.
1.2 MP sensor with large 3.75 µm pixels tuned for near-infrared, the standard 960p sensor of early HD IP cameras; also made in monochrome.
1/4-inch 1 MP (720p60) security sensor; also made in monochrome.
1 MP global-shutter sensor in colour and monochrome for scanning, tracking and AR/VR.
1080p60 security sensor with DR-Pix dual-conversion-gain pixels and on-chip multi-exposure HDR with local tone mapping.
2.3 MP global-shutter sensor at 120 fps in colour and monochrome, widely used for robotics and machine vision.
Lower-cost 1080p60 sensor with DR-Pix dual conversion gain and line-interleaved 2-exposure HDR, very common in 2 MP IP cameras; also made in an RGB-IR version.
1080p60 sensor with DR-Pix dual conversion gain and line-interleaved 2-exposure HDR, a close relative of the AR0237; also made in RGB-IR.
BSI 2.3 MP sensor at 90 fps with improved NIR response and 2- or 3-exposure line-interleaved HDR at 1080p30.
3 MP sensor first made for 1080p60 camcorders with image stabilisation, later widely used in security and USB cameras.
3 MP surveillance sensor with on-chip multi-exposure HDR and adaptive local tone mapping, 1080p60 with binning.
BSI 5 MP sensor at 60 fps with line-interleaved HDR, the replacement for the MT9P006 in security cameras; colour and monochrome.
NIR-enhanced (NIR+) version of the AR0521 for night vision; colour and monochrome.
